newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds mixed in narrow trading range.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds mixed in narrow trading range.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities were deadlocked in a narrow range on Thursday, failing to inspire heavy investor activity, traders said.

Flow was light and two-way despite the fact that mortgage yield spreads to comparable Treasuries have widened about five basis points from a week ago, said one Ginnie trader at a U.S. investment bank in New York.

"We are in a 25 basis-point range," the trader said. "If you buy a par bound in a rangebound market, the risk of dropping 25 basis points is very small," he said. The chances of picking up 25 basis points are greater, he added.
By late afternoon, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were off 2/32 at 100-20/32 bid, yielding 100 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae paper was off 1/32 at 100-16/32 bid, and Freddie Mac issues were even at 100-21/32 bid.
The five-year Treasury note was off 1/32 to yield 6.29 percent, and the 10-year Treasury note was up 1/32 to yield 6.39 percent.
